title: Personal data inside security coverage
goal: The organization brings all personal data it holds or controls, including data handled on its behalf, within the scope of its security program and policies.
note: Remainder of UC-GOV-04. Completes the generic security program for personal data.

title: Personal data access logging and review
goal: The organization logs access to personal data, reviews those logs so unauthorized access is detected and investigated, and keeps the logs and the data needed for investigation for the minimum period it is obliged to.
note: Remainder of UC-OPS-01. Carries the DPDPA log retention minimum (key setting, dpdpa layer).

title: Processor contract terms for personal data
goal: The organization binds every party that processes personal data for it, by a signed contract on file, to act only on the organization's instructions and to stop and erase that data when instructed.
note: Remainder of UC-SUP-03. Security terms themselves stay in the base control.

title: Erasure of personal data when no longer needed
goal: The organization erases personal data, and has the parties processing it for the organization erase it, once its purpose is served, consent is withdrawn or erasure is requested, unless a legal ground to keep it applies.
note: Remainder of UC-AST-08. Conditional inactivity-erasure settings (dpdpa layer) belong in the fields file.

title: Personal data retention schedule
goal: The organization sets, for each category of personal data and each purpose, a retention period or erasure trigger, names the legal ground for any retention beyond the purpose, and checks that system settings follow the schedule.

title: Breach intimation to the regulator
goal: The organization notifies the regulator of every personal data breach without delay and follows with a detailed report, in the prescribed form and content, and keeps proof that both were sent on time.
note: Remainder of UC-INC-04. Timeframes (dpdpa layer) go in key_settings only.

title: Breach notice to affected individuals
goal: The organization identifies every individual affected by a personal data breach and notifies each of them without delay with the facts, likely consequences, mitigations, steps they can take and a contact for queries.

title: Personal data breach register
goal: The organization keeps a register of every personal data breach recording the facts, effects, remedial actions and when each party was notified.

title: Notice with each consent request
goal: The organization gives every person a stand-alone notice before or with each consent request, stating what data is collected, for which purposes, how to withdraw consent and exercise rights, and how to complain to the regulator.

title: Notice and consent in the person's language
goal: The organization offers each notice and consent request in English or in the person's choice of another officially listed language.
note: Privacy-only. Number of languages is not settled by the text.

title: Notice for previously collected data
goal: The organization tells people about personal data collected before its current duties began, describing what it holds and why it is processed.

title: Published privacy contact
goal: The organization publishes, in its notices and on its website or app, the contact details of the person who answers privacy queries.

title: Consent by clear affirmative action
goal: The organization collects consent only through a clear affirmative action by the person, without pre-selected options, silence, continued use or manipulative design.

title: Consent given freely
goal: The organization keeps consent free of coercion by not making access to a service depend on processing the service does not need and by excluding terms that waive the person's rights.

title: Consent request states the purpose
goal: The organization states the specific purpose in each consent request, in clear and plain language, so that consent is informed.

title: Purpose-level consent choices
goal: The organization lists each purpose separately in the consent request and lets the person give or withhold consent for each one.
note: Privacy-only. Split from consent records (PNC-09): the test differs (consent screens versus stored records).

title: Consent records
goal: The organization keeps auditable records of when, how and for which purpose each person gave consent.

title: Fresh consent for new purposes
goal: The organization obtains fresh consent before processing personal data for a new or changed purpose.

title: Consent withdrawal
goal: The organization lets people withdraw consent as easily as they gave it.
note: Privacy-only. Split from PNC-12: ease of the channel versus effect on processing.

title: Processing stops after withdrawal
goal: The organization stops processing, and has its processors stop, within a defined period after consent is withdrawn, unless the law requires otherwise.

title: Consent manager use
goal: The organization accepts consent actions through intermediaries only where they are on the regulator's published list, and applies those actions as it would direct ones.
note: Privacy-only. Applies only where such intermediaries are used.

title: Channel for rights requests
goal: The organization publishes the means by which people can ask for access, correction, completion or erasure of their personal data, and the identifier they must give.

title: Summary of data and processing on request
goal: The organization gives a person who asks a summary of the personal data it processes, the processing activities, and the other parties it shared the data with.

title: Correction and completion
goal: The organization corrects inaccurate or misleading personal data and completes incomplete data when a person asks.

title: Erasure on request
goal: The organization erases a person's personal data when asked, and its processors do the same, unless keeping it is necessary for the purpose or required by law, and records the outcome of each request.
note: Privacy-only. Deletion mechanics are reached through AST-08 and AST-70.

title: Grievance channel and owner
goal: The organization provides an accessible way for people to raise grievances and names the person who handles them.

title: Grievance response and escalation notice
goal: The organization answers each grievance within a defined time and tells the person of the right to approach the regulator if it stays unresolved.
note: Privacy-only. Time limit (dpdpa layer) goes in key_settings if one is fixed.

title: Nomination of a representative
goal: The organization lets people nominate another individual to exercise their rights on their death or incapacity, and honors the nominee's requests.
note: Privacy-only. Home for the nomination right.

title: Processing within the consented purpose
goal: The organization processes personal data only for the purpose the person consented to.

title: Processing without consent identified and documented
goal: The organization identifies each case where it processes personal data without consent under a legitimate-use ground and documents the ground relied on.
note: Privacy-only. Related to RSK-08 (records of processing); kept apart because the test is the lawful-ground record.

title: Collection limited to what is necessary
goal: The organization collects only the personal data that is necessary for the stated purpose.

title: Accuracy of data used for decisions and disclosure
goal: The organization ensures personal data is complete, accurate and consistent before it is used for a decision affecting the person or disclosed to another party.

title: Data protection officer appointed
goal: The organization appoints a data protection officer based in India who answers to the governing body, represents the organization to the regulator and individuals, and is the named contact for grievances.
note: Privacy-only. Applies to organizations designated as significant. Base list has no equivalent role control (GOV-07 is generic).

title: Independent data auditor appointed
goal: The organization appoints an independent auditor to evaluate its compliance with its data protection duties.

title: Data protection impact assessment
goal: The organization assesses the risks of its processing activities to the people concerned, and repeats the assessment at a set interval.

title: Periodic compliance audit and report
goal: The organization has its compliance with data protection duties audited at a set interval and the auditor reports significant observations to the regulator.
note: Privacy-only. Applies to significant organizations. Close to RSK-09 but audits privacy compliance, not the security program.

title: Age verification
goal: The organization verifies the age of users so it can identify children and apply the child protections.

title: Verifiable guardian consent
goal: The organization obtains verifiable consent from a parent before processing a child's personal data, or from a lawfully appointed guardian for a person with a disability, and verifies the consenting person's identity and authority.

title: No tracking or targeting of children
goal: The organization does not track children, monitor their behavior or direct targeted advertising at them.

title: No harmful processing of children's data
goal: The organization does not process children's personal data in a way that harms their well-being.

title: Transfers only to permitted destinations
goal: The organization tracks government restrictions on destinations for personal data and does not transfer personal data to a restricted country or territory.

title: Cross-border flow inventory
goal: The organization keeps an inventory of its cross-border flows of personal data.
note: Privacy-only. May relate to AST-06 (transfer channels) but the test is the destination inventory.

title: Local storage and sectoral transfer rules
goal: The organization identifies legal requirements on where categories of personal data must be stored or may be sent, beyond the general destination rules, and complies with them.
note: Privacy-only. Applies where such requirements exist.
